questions.prompt: A gas is compressed at a constant pressure of 300 kPa from 0.21 m³ to 0.2 m³. The work done by the gas is −3 kJ.
questions.explanation: True. ΔV = 0.2 − 0.21 = −0.01 m³ is negative, so W = PΔV = −3 kJ. The work done ON the gas is 3 kJ.

questions.prompt: For an ideal gas, an isothermal process has ΔU = 0 but an adiabatic process has Q = 0.
questions.explanation: Each process removes a different term of the first law.

questions.prompt: The efficiency of a heat engine can also be written η = 1 − T₁/T₂.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is Q₂/Q₁. η = (Q₁ − Q₂)/Q₁ = 1 − Q₂/Q₁.

questions.prompt: In an adiabatic expansion the temperature of the gas becomes infinite.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is falls. The gas does work at the expense of its internal energy.

questions.prompt: Sound passing through air is an example of an isothermal process.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is adiabatic. The compressions and rarefactions are too fast for heat exchange.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine works between 600 K and 300 K and absorbs 1200 J of heat per cycle. The work done per cycle is 600 J.
A Carnot engine works between a source at 800 K and a sink at 250 K. The efficiency is 68.8%.
A fixed mass of gas occupies 6 L at 6 atm. It is compressed isothermally to 10 atm. The final volume is 10 L.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 3.6 L. Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = (6 × 6)/10 = 3.6 L.

questions.prompt: Condensation of steam increases the entropy of the substance.
questions.explanation: False: the molecules become more ordered, so entropy decreases.

questions.prompt: In a reversible process, if heat is absorbed in the direct process, it is destroyed in the reverse process.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is evolved. Heat flow and work reverse their directions.

questions.prompt: A thermos flask of hot water is an open system.
questions.explanation: False: neither heat nor mass crosses its boundary, so it is an isolated system.

questions.prompt: The matter or region of space under study in thermodynamics is called the system.
questions.explanation: The system is what we study; everything outside it is the surroundings.

questions.prompt: The efficiency of a petrol engine is roughly 90% to 95%.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is 25% to 30%. Most of the fuel energy is expelled to the atmosphere.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of heat is the watt.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is joule. Heat is a form of energy, so its SI unit is the joule (J).

questions.prompt: In an isochoric process the volume stays constant.
questions.explanation: By definition.

questions.prompt: Doubling the absolute temperature of an ideal gas quadruples the average kinetic energy of a molecule.

questions.prompt: Heat flows naturally in only one direction, from warm to hot to cold.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is hot. The tea in an air-conditioned room cools but never warms back by itself.

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs 800 J of heat and does 200 J of work. The change in internal energy is 1000 J.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 600 J. Q = ΔU + W, so ΔU = Q − W = 800 − 200 = 600 J.

questions.prompt: A system gives out 900 J of heat reversibly at a constant temperature of 300 K. The change in entropy is −3 J K⁻¹.

questions.prompt: The collisions between the molecules of an ideal gas are perfectly sticky.

questions.prompt: The average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is given by (3/2)kT.

questions.prompt: Friction increases the entropy of a system.

questions.prompt: Doing work on a gas while no heat escapes (Q = 0) makes its internal energy increase.

questions.prompt: The net work in one Carnot cycle is the perimeter enclosed by the cycle on the P–V diagram.

questions.prompt: In an isochoric process all the heat supplied goes into internal energy.

questions.prompt: A gas is compressed at a constant pressure of 500 kPa from 0.32 m³ to 0.02 m³. The work done by the gas is −150 kJ.
questions.explanation: True. ΔV = 0.02 − 0.32 = −0.3 m³ is negative, so W = PΔV = −150 kJ. The work done ON the gas is 150 kJ.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator used to heat a space that is warmer than its surroundings is called a heat engine.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is heat pump. The same device in heating mode.

questions.prompt: In a refrigerator the heat rejected to the room is Q₁ = Q₂ + W.
questions.explanation: Energy balance.

questions.prompt: A gas in a rigid vessel is at 1 atm and 227 °C. It is cooled to 27 °C. The final pressure is 0.119 atm.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 0.6 atm. Volume is constant: P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 1 × 300/500 = 0.6 atm (T in kelvin).

questions.prompt: In Q = ΔU + W, Q is positive when heat is removed from the system.
questions.explanation: False: Q is positive when heat is added.

questions.prompt: PV = NkT and PV = nRT express the same law.
questions.explanation: n = N/N_A and k = R/N_A convert one into the other.

questions.prompt: When heat flows from a hot body to a cold body the net entropy change is positive.
questions.explanation: Q/T₂ is larger than Q/T₁ since T₁ > T₂.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator is a heat engine working in reverse.
questions.explanation: Work is done to move heat from cold to hot.

questions.prompt: When heat flows from a hot body to a cold body the net entropy increases.
questions.explanation: ΔS = Q/T₂ − Q/T₁ > 0.

questions.prompt: For an ideal refrigerator CP (cooling) = T₂/(T₁ − T₂).
questions.explanation: From Q₂/(Q₁ − Q₂) with Q ∝ T.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin.
questions.explanation: Temperature is measured in kelvin (K); the joule is the unit of heat.

questions.prompt: Two systems are in thermal equilibrium when they are at the same temperature.
questions.explanation: Equal temperature is the only condition for thermal equilibrium.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine works between 57 °C and 7 °C. The efficiency is 15.2%.
questions.explanation: True. T₁ = 330 K, T₂ = 280 K; η = 1 − T₂/T₁ = 1 − 280/330 = 15.2%. Temperatures must be in kelvin.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator can cool its inside without any work input.
questions.explanation: False: heat does not flow from cold to hot by itself.

questions.prompt: In an adiabatic process no heat is transferred.
The Carnot cycle consists of two isothermal and two adiabatic processes.
questions.explanation: Isothermal expansion, adiabatic expansion, isothermal compression, adiabatic compression.

questions.prompt: The internal energy of an ideal gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature.
questions.explanation: ⟨K.E.⟩ = (3/2)kT so U ∝ T.

questions.prompt: The first law for an isothermal process becomes Q = W.
questions.explanation: With ΔU = 0, all heat supplied becomes work.

questions.prompt: Two bodies at the same temperature always contain the same amount of heat energy.
questions.explanation: False: heat depends on the number of molecules as well as temperature, so a bigger body holds more heat.

questions.prompt: The work output of a heat engine per cycle is W = Q₁ − Q₂.
questions.explanation: Heat absorbed minus heat rejected.

questions.prompt: A gas expands at a constant pressure of 500 kPa from 0.05 m³ to 0.2 m³. The work done by the gas is 75 kJ.
questions.explanation: True. W = PΔV = 500 kPa × (0.2 − 0.05) m³ = 75 kJ (positive, work done by the gas).

questions.prompt: The average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is (3/2)kT.
questions.explanation: This is Eq. 8.1 of the unit.

questions.prompt: A gas expands at a constant pressure of 150 kPa from 0.02 m³ to 0.52 m³. The work done by the gas is 75 kJ.
questions.explanation: True. W = PΔV = 150 kPa × (0.52 − 0.02) m³ = 75 kJ (positive, work done by the gas).

questions.prompt: In Q = ΔU + W, W is the work done by the system.
questions.explanation: Work done by the gas on its surroundings is positive.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine can reach 100% efficiency if its sink is at 0 °C.
questions.explanation: False: 0 °C is 273 K; 100% would need a sink at absolute zero.

questions.prompt: A system absorbs 1200 J of heat reversibly at a constant temperature of 250 K. The change in entropy is 4.8 J K⁻¹.
questions.explanation: True. ΔS = ΔQ/T = 1200/250 = 4.8 J K⁻¹ (positive because heat is added).

questions.prompt: The pressure of a gas is made 5 times larger at constant temperature. The factor by which its volume changes is 0.04 times.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 0.2 times. PV = constant, so V becomes 1/5 of its value.

questions.prompt: On a P–V diagram an adiabat is steeper than an isotherm.
questions.explanation: The gas cools as it expands, so the pressure drops faster.

questions.prompt: Oxygen (molar mass 32 g mol⁻¹) is treated as an ideal gas at 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa and 400 K. (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) The density is 0.975 kg m⁻³.
questions.explanation: True. ρ = PM/(RT) = (1.013 × 10⁵ × 0.032)/(8.314 × 400) = 0.975 kg m⁻³ (molar mass in kg mol⁻¹).

questions.prompt: Kelvin's statement says an engine cannot turn heat from a single reservoir entirely into work.
questions.explanation: This is the Kelvin form of the second law.

questions.prompt: The temperatures used in Carnot efficiency must be in kelvin.
questions.explanation: Using °C gives a wrong ratio.

questions.prompt: An isothermal process must be carried out rapidly.
questions.explanation: False: it must be slow so that heat can flow and keep T constant.

questions.prompt: Boyle's law states that PV is constant for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature.
A refrigerator needs work because heat does not flow from cold to hot by itself.
questions.explanation: This is Clausius's statement.

questions.prompt: 1 mol of an ideal gas at 300 K occupies 20 L. (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) The pressure is 49.9 kPa.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 125 kPa. PV = nRT, so P = nRT/V = (1 × 8.314 × 300)/20 = 125 kPa (J per L = kPa).

questions.prompt: A gas in a rigid vessel is at 8 atm and 227 °C. It is cooled to 127 °C. The final pressure is 12.8 atm.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 6.4 atm. Volume is constant: P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 8 × 400/500 = 6.4 atm (T in kelvin).

questions.prompt: The working principle of a heat engine is based on the second law of thermodynamics.
questions.explanation: Work is obtained during heat transfer from hot to cold.

questions.prompt: A system absorbs 840 J of heat reversibly at a constant temperature of 350 K. The change in entropy is 2.4 J K⁻¹.
questions.explanation: True. ΔS = ΔQ/T = 840/350 = 2.4 J K⁻¹ (positive because heat is added).

questions.prompt: Gas pressure is caused by collisions of the molecules with the container walls.
questions.explanation: Impacts on the walls give the pressure.

questions.prompt: A real gas behaves most like an ideal gas at high pressure and low temperature.
questions.explanation: False: it behaves ideally at low pressure and high temperature.

questions.prompt: Heating a gas at constant volume raises its pressure because its molecules hit the walls harder and more often.
questions.explanation: Higher average K.E. means stronger and more frequent impacts.

questions.prompt: Argon (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) is treated as an ideal gas at 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa and 273 K. (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) The density is 17.9 kg m⁻³.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 1.79 kg m⁻³. ρ = PM/(RT) = (1.013 × 10⁵ × 0.04)/(8.314 × 273) = 1.79 kg m⁻³ (molar mass in kg mol⁻¹).

questions.prompt: The hot reservoir of a heat engine is also called the source.
questions.explanation: It supplies the heat Q₁.

questions.prompt: Charles's law is stated at constant temperature.
questions.explanation: False: Charles's law holds at constant pressure.

questions.prompt: A heat engine takes 1200 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 960 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. The efficiency is 20%.
A succession of events that brings a system back to its initial condition is a isobaric process.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is cyclic. The system returns to the starting state.

questions.prompt: A system in which neither heat nor mass crosses the boundary is an isolated system.
questions.explanation: A thermos flask of hot water is the standard example of an isolated system.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine works between 800 K and 400 K and absorbs 1200 J of heat per cycle. The work done per cycle is 600 J.
At the same temperature and pressure, one mole of any ideal gas contains N_A molecules; N_A is called the Avogadro number.
questions.explanation: N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ per mole.

questions.prompt: The work done by a gas that is compressed is positive.
questions.explanation: False: ΔV < 0, so the work done by the gas is negative.

questions.prompt: 1900 J of heat is supplied to a gas in a rigid (fixed-volume) container. The change in internal energy is 1900 J.
questions.explanation: True. Volume is constant, so W = 0 and ΔU = Q = 1900 J.

questions.prompt: A gas of volume 8 L at 227 °C is heated to 327 °C at constant pressure. The final volume is 9.6 L.
questions.explanation: True. Charles's law with kelvin: V₂ = V₁T₂/T₁ = 8 × 600/500 = 9.6 L.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine is a theoretical engine working on a reversible cycle.
questions.explanation: It is an ideal engine, not a real one.

questions.prompt: No engine working between the same two temperatures is more efficient than a Carnot engine.
questions.explanation: This is Carnot's theorem.

questions.prompt: The work done by a gas at constant pressure is W = PΔV.
questions.explanation: Pressure times change in volume.

questions.prompt: Extending the V–T line of a gas backwards, it meets the temperature axis at −373 °C.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is −273 °C. The volume would reduce to zero at −273 °C.

questions.prompt: The curve of an isobaric process is called an isobar.
questions.explanation: A horizontal line on the P–V graph.

questions.prompt: A gas expands by 0.003 m³ at a constant pressure of 500 kPa while it absorbs 6.0 kJ of heat. The change in internal energy is 4.5 kJ.
Pumping air into a tyre warms the pump because work done on the air raises its potential energy.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is internal. The work compresses the air and increases its internal energy.

questions.prompt: In an isobaric process the pressure stays constant.
questions.explanation: By definition.

questions.prompt: 360 J of work is done on a gas while it is compressed adiabatically. The change in its internal energy is 360 J.
questions.explanation: True. Q = 0 and the work done by the gas is −360 J, so ΔU = −(−360) = +360 J: the gas warms up.

questions.prompt: Melting of ice at 0 °C is an example of an isothermal process.
questions.explanation: The temperature stays at 0 °C.

questions.prompt: In the adiabatic compression step the temperature of the gas rises from T₂ to T₂/2.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is T₁. The gas returns to its initial state.

questions.prompt: The internal energy of a system can rise while its temperature stays the same.
questions.explanation: During melting or boiling the energy goes into potential energy of the particles.

questions.prompt: In an isobaric process the pressure of the system stays constant.
questions.explanation: Isobaric means constant pressure.

questions.prompt: In an isothermal process the temperature stays constant.
questions.explanation: By definition.

questions.prompt: The unit of entropy is J K⁻¹.
questions.explanation: ΔS = ΔQ/T.

questions.prompt: For an ideal gas the internal energy is directly proportional to the absolute temperature.
questions.explanation: U is proportional to T, because average K.E. = (3/2)kT.

questions.prompt: When the volume of a gas stays constant, no work is done.
questions.explanation: ΔV = 0 gives W = 0.

questions.prompt: A cup of hot tea in a cool room will warm back up by itself.
questions.explanation: False: heat flows only from hot to cold.

questions.prompt: The same device used to heat a warm space is called a heat pump.
questions.explanation: It is the refrigerator cycle used for heating.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of heat is the kelvin.
questions.explanation: False: the SI unit of heat is the joule; the kelvin is the unit of temperature.

questions.prompt: If heat is removed from a gas at constant volume, both its temperature and pressure decrease.
questions.explanation: Gay-Lussac: P ∝ T at constant volume.

questions.prompt: Any process involving friction is reversible.
questions.explanation: False: friction makes a process irreversible.

questions.prompt: The litre-atmosphere is a unit of pressure.
questions.explanation: False: it is a unit of work (pressure × volume).

questions.prompt: The unit of the Boltzmann constant is J K⁻¹.
questions.explanation: It is the same as the unit of entropy.

questions.prompt: The inside of an ideal refrigerator is at 3 °C and the room is at 37 °C. Each joule of electrical work is supplied to the compressor. The heat delivered to the room per joule of work is 9.12 J.
questions.explanation: True. T₁ = 310 K, T₂ = 276 K; Q₁/W = CP (heating) = T₁/(T₁ − T₂) = 310/34 = 9.12 J.

questions.prompt: A gas does 500 J of work in an adiabatic expansion. The change in its internal energy is 0 J.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is −500 J. Q = 0, so ΔU = −W = −500 J: the internal energy decreases and the gas cools.

questions.prompt: The ideal gas equation is PV = nRT.
questions.explanation: It links pressure, volume, moles and temperature.

questions.prompt: The net entropy change of a Carnot engine over one cycle is zero.
questions.explanation: It is reversible and returns to its initial state.

questions.prompt: Gay-Lussac's law can be written as P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂.
questions.explanation: P/T is constant at constant volume.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator that works without any work input would violate Clausius's statement.
questions.explanation: Clausius's statement forbids heat flowing from cold to hot without work.

questions.prompt: A heat engine works in straight lines so that it can run continuously.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is cycles. The working substance returns to its initial state each cycle.

questions.prompt: The gas laws can be used with temperature in °C without any change.
questions.explanation: False: temperature must be in kelvin.

questions.prompt: Two systems in thermal equilibrium are at the same temperature.
questions.explanation: Equal temperature is the condition for thermal equilibrium.

questions.prompt: In kinetic theory the size of the molecules is much larger than their separation.
questions.explanation: False: molecules are much smaller than the distance between them.

questions.prompt: A diathermic substance does not allow heat to pass through it.
questions.explanation: False: a diathermic substance allows heat to pass.

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs 400 J of heat and does 700 J of work. The change in internal energy is −300 J.
questions.explanation: True. Q = ΔU + W, so ΔU = Q − W = 400 − 700 = −300 J.

questions.prompt: In terms of the number of molecules N, the ideal gas equation is PV = N/kT.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is NkT. With n = N/N_A and k = R/N_A, PV = NkT.

questions.prompt: A system gives out 2000 J of heat reversibly at a constant temperature of 400 K. The change in entropy is −5 J K⁻¹.
questions.explanation: True. Heat is removed, so ΔQ = −2000 J and ΔS = ΔQ/T = −2000/400 = −5 J K⁻¹ (negative).

questions.prompt: An ideal gas is at 17 °C. (k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹) The average translational kinetic energy of a molecule is 4 × 10⁻²¹ J.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 6 × 10⁻²¹ J. T = 17 + 273 = 290 K and ⟨K.E.⟩ = (3/2)kT = 1.5 × 1.38 × 10⁻²³ × 290 = 6 × 10⁻²¹ J.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine works between 1000 K and 400 K and absorbs 400 J of heat per cycle. The work done per cycle is 160 J.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 240 J. η = 1 − 400/1000; W = ηQ₁ = 0.6 × 400 = 240 J.

questions.prompt: The inside of an ideal refrigerator is at 10 °C and the room is at 32 °C. Each joule of electrical work is supplied to the compressor. The heat delivered to the room per joule of work is 13.9 J.
questions.explanation: True. T₁ = 305 K, T₂ = 283 K; Q₁/W = CP (heating) = T₁/(T₁ − T₂) = 305/22 = 13.9 J.

questions.prompt: An adiabatic process occurs at constant volume, leaving no time for heat to enter or leave.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is rapidly. Rapid change keeps Q = 0.

questions.prompt: In a refrigerator the entropy of the universe still vanishes even though the inside is cooled.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is increases. The room warms more than the inside cools.

questions.prompt: The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of the law of conservation of energy.
questions.explanation: Heat supplied goes into internal energy and work.

questions.prompt: A gas expands by 0.002 m³ at a constant pressure of 500 kPa while it absorbs 3.0 kJ of heat. The change in internal energy is 4 kJ.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 2 kJ. W = PΔV = 500 × 0.002 = 1 kJ and ΔU = Q − W = 3.0 − 1 = 2 kJ.

questions.prompt: Clausius's statement says heat can flow from cold to hot without any work.
questions.explanation: False: heat cannot flow from cold to hot without work.

questions.prompt: A heat engine takes 400 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 200 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. The efficiency is 50%.
The P–V graph of an isobaric process is a horizontal line.
questions.explanation: Pressure is fixed.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator removes heat from a region that is colder than its surroundings.
questions.explanation: It cools the inside by pushing heat to the room.

questions.prompt: For an ideal gas at constant temperature the density is proportional to the pressure.
questions.explanation: ρ = PM/RT.

questions.prompt: A system gives out 2730 J of heat reversibly at a constant temperature of 500 K. The change in entropy is 5.46 J K⁻¹.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is −5.46 J K⁻¹. Heat is removed, so ΔQ = −2730 J and ΔS = ΔQ/T = −2730/500 = −5.46 J K⁻¹ (negative).

questions.prompt: The entropy of water increases when ice melts.
questions.explanation: The molecules lose their order.

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs 800 J of heat and does 400 J of work. The change in internal energy is 1200 J.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 400 J. Q = ΔU + W, so ΔU = Q − W = 800 − 400 = 400 J.

questions.prompt: The P–V graph of a gas at constant temperature is a straight line.
questions.explanation: False: it is a hyperbola, since PV = constant.

questions.prompt: The universal gas constant R has the value 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
questions.explanation: R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

questions.prompt: Entropy stays constant for reversible processes.
questions.explanation: Only irreversible processes raise entropy.

questions.prompt: A gas expands at a constant pressure of 100 kPa from 0.01 m³ to 0.16 m³. The work done by the gas is 1 kJ.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 15 kJ. W = PΔV = 100 kPa × (0.16 − 0.01) m³ = 15 kJ (positive, work done by the gas).

questions.prompt: Heat flows from a hotter body to a colder body when they are in contact.
questions.explanation: Heat always flows from higher to lower temperature until equilibrium is reached.

questions.prompt: In terms of entropy the second law says the entropy of the system plus the environment increases in a natural process.
questions.explanation: Natural processes proceed in the direction of increasing total entropy.

questions.prompt: The Boltzmann constant is equal to R multiplied by N_A.
questions.explanation: False: k = R/N_A.

questions.prompt: An ideal gas is at 227 °C. (k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹) The average translational kinetic energy of a molecule is 2.07 × 10⁻²⁰ J.
In the adiabatic expansion of the Carnot cycle the temperature falls from T₁ to T₂.
questions.explanation: The gas cools to the sink temperature T₂.

questions.prompt: In one complete cycle a gas absorbs 400 J of heat and rejects 450 J of heat. The net work done by the gas in the cycle is 0 J.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is −50 J. Over a cycle ΔU = 0, so W = Q = 400 − 450 = -50 J.

questions.prompt: 1000 g of ice melts at 0 °C. (Latent heat of fusion = 3.36 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹) The increase in entropy is 1230 J K⁻¹.
An ideal gas is at 427 °C. (k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹) The average translational kinetic energy of a molecule is 2.9 × 10⁻²⁰ J.
The V–T line of a gas at constant pressure meets the temperature axis at −273 °C when extended.
questions.explanation: The volume would reduce to zero there.

questions.prompt: Heat flows naturally from a body at higher temperature to a body at lower temperature.
questions.explanation: Heat always flows from hot to cold until the temperatures become equal.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine has its sink at 300 K and its source at 1200 K. The source temperature is doubled. The factor by which the efficiency increases (new η / old η) is 0.857 times.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 1.17 times. Old η = 1 − 300/1200 = 0.75; new η = 1 − 300/2400 = 0.875; ratio = 1.17.

questions.prompt: Hydrogen (molar mass 2 g mol⁻¹) is treated as an ideal gas at 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa and 400 K. (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) The density is 0.0609 kg m⁻³.
questions.explanation: True. ρ = PM/(RT) = (1.013 × 10⁵ × 0.002)/(8.314 × 400) = 0.0609 kg m⁻³ (molar mass in kg mol⁻¹).

questions.prompt: The order of the four strokes of a petrol engine is intake, compression, power, exhaust.
questions.explanation: This is the standard sequence.

questions.prompt: An increase in entropy means degradation of energy.
questions.explanation: Part of the energy becomes unavailable for work.

questions.prompt: The first step of the Carnot cycle is isothermal expansion at the higher temperature T₁.
questions.explanation: The gas absorbs heat Q₁ from the hot reservoir.

questions.prompt: A device that converts heat energy into mechanical work is a heat engine.
questions.explanation: A heat engine turns heat into work.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator cools its inside, so the total entropy of the universe decreases.
questions.explanation: False: the entropy of the room rises by more than the inside loses.

questions.prompt: 1.5 mol of an ideal gas at 500 K occupies 50 L. (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) The pressure is 56.6 kPa.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 125 kPa. PV = nRT, so P = nRT/V = (1.5 × 8.314 × 500)/50 = 125 kPa (J per L = kPa).

questions.prompt: The temperature of a gas is 77 °C. The temperature on the kelvin scale (use T = t + 273) is 350 K.
A gas gives out 400 J of heat while 200 J of work is done on it. The change in internal energy is −200 J.
questions.explanation: True. Q = −400 J and the work done by the gas is W = −200 J, so ΔU = Q − W = −400 − (−200) = −200 J.

questions.prompt: The first law of thermodynamics is the law of conservation of energy applied to heat and work.
questions.explanation: Q = ΔU + W.

questions.prompt: The absolute temperature of an ideal gas changes from 400 K to 1600 K. The factor by which the average K.E. of a molecule changes is 2 times.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 4 times. ⟨K.E.⟩ ∝ T, so the factor is 1600/400 = 4.

questions.prompt: A fixed mass of gas occupies 24 L at 5 atm. It is compressed isothermally to 10 atm. The final volume is 29 L.
questions.explanation: False — the correct value is 12 L. Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = (5 × 24)/10 = 12 L.

questions.prompt: The Boltzmann constant k equals N_A/R.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is R/N_A. k = R/N_A is the gas constant per molecule.

questions.prompt: The "arrow of time" is related to the volume of an isolated system.
questions.explanation: False — the correct answer is entropy. Entropy increases with time, so it tells past from future.

questions.prompt: Boyle's, Charles's and Gay-Lussac's laws all follow from PV = nRT.
questions.explanation: Hold n fixed and keep one of P, V or T constant.

questions.prompt: Boiling of water in an open vessel is an isobaric process.
questions.explanation: The pressure stays at atmospheric pressure.

questions.prompt: If the temperature of a system falls, the change in internal energy ΔU is negative.
questions.explanation: U2 < U1 when T falls, so ΔU is negative.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator is a heat engine operating in reverse.
questions.explanation: Work is done to move heat from cold to hot.

questions.prompt: Raising the temperature of the source raises the Carnot efficiency when the sink stays fixed.
questions.explanation: T₂/T₁ becomes smaller.

questions.prompt: The entropy of a system decreases when heat is added to it.
questions.explanation: False: ΔS = ΔQ/T is positive when heat is added.

questions.prompt: When a gas expands, the work done by the gas is positive.
questions.explanation: ΔV > 0 gives W = PΔV > 0.

questions.prompt: The area under a constant-pressure line on a P–V graph is a rectangle.
questions.explanation: Width ΔV and height P give area PΔV.
